record.paper_title: Open Problems About Sumsets in Finite Abelian Groups: Minimum Sizes and Critical Numbers
record.original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and for an m-element subset A={a1,...,am} define hA as the set of all sums λ1a1+...+λm am with nonnegative integer coefficients summing to h. Define ρ(G,m,h) as the minimum possible value of |hA| over all m-element subsets A of G. In the boundary case p = hm - h + 1, classify all m-element subsets A of G for which |hA|=ρ(G,m,h). In particular, determine all extremal subsets beyond the known possibilities of arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p.

evidence.quote: the h-fold sumset: hA = {Σ_i=1^m λ_i ai | λ1,...,λm ∈ N0, Σ_i=1^m λi = h}
ρ (G, m, h) = min{|hA| | A ⊆ G, |A| = m}

This leaves the case when p = hm − h + 1, where arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets in a coset of a subgroup of order p are two of several possibilities. It may be an interesting problem to classify all such subsets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, written additively, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a finite subset $A = \{a_1, \dots, a_m\} \subseteq G$ of size $m$ and a positive integer $h$, define the $h$-fold sumset of $A$ by
$$hA = \Big\{ \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i a_i \;\Big|\; \lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\ \sum_{i=1}^m \lambda_i = h \Big\}.$$
Define
$$\rho(G, m, h) = \min\{\,|hA| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\,\}.$$
Assume the boundary equality $p = hm - h + 1$. Classify all $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ that attain $|hA| = \rho(G, m, h)$. In particular, characterize all such extremal subsets beyond the two known families:
(i) arithmetic progressions of length $m$ in $G$, and
(ii) $m$-element subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of $G$ of order $p$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published classification of the extremal sets in the boundary case $p = hm-h+1$ was located. The question is posed as an open classification problem; searches for inverse results on $\rho(G,m,h)$ in this regime returned only general background on sumsets in abelian groups and no resolution of the boundary case.

status_evidence.title: Sumsets and structure - Ruzsa
status_evidence.snippet: General reference on sumset inverse problems in abelian groups; does not address the specific boundary classification.
status_evidence.claim: Background on additive combinatorics; no resolution of the boundary classification is given.

status_evidence.title: Zero-sum problems in finite abelian groups: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of zero-sum and sumset problems in finite abelian groups.
status_evidence.claim: No classification of extremal $m$-sets in the boundary case $p=hm-h+1$ is recorded.
